name: Sledgehammer Lever (Forearm Levering)
description: The sledgehammer lever involves holding a sledgehammer at the very end of its handle with one hand extended and slowly lowering it forward or to the side from a vertical position, then raising it back — using wrist and forearm strength to control the extreme lever arm. The long handle creates significant torque on the forearm even with a lightweight hammer, making it one of the most effective single-tool wrist extensor exercises.

execution.starting_position: Hold a sledgehammer at the very end of the handle with one hand, arm at the side, hammer vertical with head up.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a 2-4kg sledgehammer. The lever arm is the challenge, not the head weight. Stand with feet hip-width.
steps: Step 1: Hold the hammer vertical, arm extended slightly forward.
Step 2: Slowly lower the hammer forward (or to the side) by extending the wrist, controlling the lever.
Step 3: Lower as far as wrist control allows without losing the grip.
Step 4: Raise the hammer back to vertical using wrist flexion.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the lower.
common_mistakes: Gripping too close to the head — the grip must be at the very end of the handle
safety_considerations: Start with a light hammer — the lever arm is deceptively difficult
Perform over a rubber mat in case of drop
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Vertical to horizontal (or as far as controlled).
coaching_cues: Grip the very end of the handle
Slow and controlled in both directions
